extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers interested in postwar international and domestic affairs
extracted.subtask_description: A wire-service news-article compilation reporting post‑World War II military/governmental developments, occupation policy updates, labor dispute hearings, and trials — suitable for a news homepage or front‑page placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-finding board obligation to develop facts and submit recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: “The obligation of the fact-finding board is to develop, to the best of its ability, the facts relevant to the General Motors-U. A. W. dispute, and to submit these facts to the President, with such recommendations as the board may deem appropriate.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board must gather and present a thorough factual record and recommendations; accomplishing this requires cooperation from both parties, and the board has two alternatives if cooperation is lacking—report inability to proceed or proceed using available evidence and do its best.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for whole‑hearted cooperation of both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: “To do this as thoroughly and reliably as the President and the public have a right to expect, the board needs the whole‑hearted co‑operation of both parties to the dispute.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either side withholds cooperation or information the board may either report it cannot proceed or continue on the basis of available evidence; cooperation is therefore an explicit procedural expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to pay is relevant but not the sole controlling factor
rubrics_metrics.description: “Ability to pay will not be regarded as the only or controlling factor in determining the amount of a fair and equitable wage adjustment.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board will consider ability to pay among other factors (wage history, economic context), but it will focus on determining a fair wage rather than fixing profits; ability to pay should be weighed, not dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board’s focus on fair wage, not fixing profits
rubrics_metrics.description: “The board is not concerned with fixing profits but only with the question of what is a fair wage.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In deliberations the fact‑finding board frames its remit as finding a fair wage recommendation for the President rather than adjudicating corporate profit levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to inquire into union loss-of-take-home-pay calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: “The board's first task is to inquire into these calculations” (referring to the union’s figure derived from calculations relating to loss of take‑home pay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board should request and evaluate the calculations and supporting data used by the union to justify wage demands; such evidence is a central part of the board’s factual inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for company financial information to assess ability to pay and inflationary effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The board stated it needs a reasonably adequate picture of the company’s financial situation (books, wage rates, hours, earning capacity) in order to satisfy itself that any wage adjustment recommended will not have inflationary price consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for company financial records, wage/hour data, and related information are procedural necessities; if the company withholds such information the board will proceed on available evidence but notes that withholding impairs the board’s ability to assess inflationary impact and ability to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two operational alternatives when evidence/cooperation is lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: If the board lacks cooperation or necessary evidence it has only two alternatives: report to the President that it was unable to proceed or do the very best it can on the basis of evidence that is or will be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural rubric clarifies how the board will proceed under uncooperative circumstances and sets expectations about the completeness and limits of any resulting report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of a minimum sustaining economy for Germany requires treating Germany as a single economic unit
rubrics_metrics.description: McNarney: “Restoration of a minimum sustaining economy is most difficult if not impossible as long as artificial zonal boundaries restrict legitimate movement and trade.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy for restoring Germany should prioritize treating the country as a single economic unit and removing artificial zonal restrictions on movement and trade to allow legitimate economic activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish an assumed standard of living and required industrial level for postwar Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: McNarney: One of the main issues is establishing an assumed standard of living in postwar Germany and the level of industry required to maintain that standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occupation/reparations planning must define a target standard of living and then determine the industrial capacity and production levels necessary to sustain that standard — this standard drives reparations and reinstatement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food import metric for German subsistence
rubrics_metrics.description: “Food imports from the United States provided the only way a 1,500 daily caloric diet could be maintained…during November most people were able to supplement the official ration, so that the normal consumer was getting about 1,900 calories on the average.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caloric intake targets (e.g., 1,500 baseline sustained by imports, 1,900 with supplements) are used as benchmarks for food policy and relief planning; maintaining these levels informs import and distribution decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial recovery metrics (authorization and output levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Through December 1 about 33 per cent of the plants in the United States zone were authorized to resume production, but shortages in transportation, coal and power limited industrial production to from 5 to 10 per cent of normal capacity.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industrial recovery should be measured by percent of plants authorized to operate and actual output relative to normal capacity; logistics and fuel constraints are identified limiting factors to be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing industrial capital equipment for reparations and declaring plants available
rubrics_metrics.description: “The four occupying powers are making good progress in listing industrial capital equipment for reparations…Eighty‑four plants in the three Western zones have already been declared available for reparations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A procedural standard for reparations: inventory industrial capital equipment and designate which plants/equipment are available for reparations; these lists feed decisions about industrial capacity and standards of living.
